sections.search: Getting started What happens the first time you sign in, and how to set up your new workspace. Başlarken İlk kez giriş yaptığınızda ne olur ve yeni çalışma alanınızı nasıl kurarsınız.

sections.title: Setting up your workspace when you first sign in
sections.path: Getting started › Setting up your workspace when you first sign in
sections.text:
When you first open NivaDesk, a five-step setup gets your workspace ready for your kind of work. There is no Skip: every step is answerable, and the step that asks how you want to start offers "Start empty" and "I'll set this up later" as real choices. Back is there from step two onwards.
The setup runs once per workspace. If you have already been through it, everything it set is in Settings.

İlk girişte çalışma alanınızı kurma NivaDesk'i ilk açtığınızda beş adımlık bir kurulum, çalışma alanınızı yaptığınız işe göre hazırlar. Atlama (Skip) yoktur: her adım cevaplanabilir ve nasıl başlamak istediğinizi soran adımda "Boş başla" ile "Bunu sonra ayarlayacağım" gerçek birer seçenektir. Geri düğmesi ikinci adımdan itibaren hep oradadır.
Kurulum her çalışma alanı için bir kez çalışır. Daha önce geçtiyseniz, kurduğu her şey Settings içindedir.

sections.title: What your setup answers change
sections.path: Getting started › What your setup answers change
sections.text:
The questions are not a survey: each answer changes the workspace you get.
Nothing here is permanent: your business type, workflow steps, labels and production stages can all be changed later in Settings.

sections.title: Your free trial and plans
sections.text: What signing up costs, when the paid trial starts, and what happens when it ends.
sections.search: Your free trial and plans What signing up costs, when the paid trial starts, and what happens when it ends. Ücretsiz denemeniz ve planlar Kaydolmanın maliyeti, ücretli denemenin ne zaman başladığı ve bittiğinde ne olduğu.

sections.title: No credit card to sign up
sections.path: Your free trial and plans › No credit card to sign up
sections.text:
You do not need a credit card to sign up for NivaDesk, and no payment details are asked for anywhere in setup. The Free plan never expires: 10 active orders, 10 customers, your personal notes and export access, at no cost and with no time limit.
The 14-day trial of the paid plan is separate, and it does not start when you register.

Free planın süresi hiç dolmaz: 10 aktif sipariş, 10 müşteri, kişisel notlarınız ve dışa aktarma erişimi; ücretsiz ve süresiz.
Ücretli planın 14 günlük denemesi bundan ayrıdır ve kaydolduğunuzda başlamaz.

sections.title: When the 14-day trial starts
sections.path: Your free trial and plans › When the 14-day trial starts
sections.text:
- It starts when you create your first order — not at sign-up, so the fortnight is spent working rather than looking around.
- It runs on Pro, or on Team if you said more than one person would use NivaDesk during setup.
- No credit card is taken and no subscription is created. Nothing renews and nothing can be charged.
- A banner shows what is left, and what the trial has been worth so far. It collapses if you would rather not see it.
Each workspace gets one trial, so starting a paid plan at checkout does not add another fortnight on top.

Her çalışma alanına bir deneme verilir; ödeme sayfasından ücretli plan başlatmak üstüne ikinci bir iki hafta eklemez.

sections.title: What happens when the trial ends
sections.path: Your free trial and plans › What happens when the trial ends
sections.text:
The workspace goes back to Free, and a notice says so plainly with "Continue on Free" and "Choose a plan" side by side. Nothing is deleted: every order, customer, file and note stays visible and exportable.
What stops is the paid-plan features — Client Files, advanced finance, team messaging — and creating new orders beyond the Free limit of 10 active ones. Archiving finished orders brings you back under the limit. NivaDesk never decides which of your orders to keep.
Upgrading later picks everything up exactly where it stopped.

sections.title: Where your plan is billed, and why you can only buy in one place
sections.path: Your free trial and plans › Where your plan is billed, and why you can only buy in one place
sections.text:
A NivaDesk plan can be paid for in four places: by card on the website, through the App Store on Mac and iPhone, through Google Play on Android, or on your Shopify invoice if you installed us from the Shopify App Store. Whichever one you used is the only place that plan can be changed.
- The plan page in every app tells you where your subscription lives, and does not offer to sell you the same plan a second time — buying again somewhere else would mean two companies charging you for one workspace, and neither of them would know about the other.
- To move to a different plan, change it where you already pay: the website Billing portal, your Apple subscriptions, your Google Play subscriptions, or the NivaDesk app inside your Shopify admin.
- To move to a different place, cancel the subscription you have first, then buy again where you want it. Your workspace and everything in it stay exactly as they are.
- Changing tier where you already pay — Lite to Pro, monthly to yearly — is a normal upgrade and works as it always did.
- Extra storage and extra team seats are add-ons, not plans. They are sold wherever you are, whichever place your plan is billed.

sections.title: Monthly and yearly billing
sections.path: Your free trial and plans › Monthly and yearly billing
sections.text:
Yearly billing is ten months' price for twelve. The plan page shows the monthly equivalent and the exact amount saved beside each yearly price — Pro is £190 a year, which is £15.83 a month and £38 saved — so you can compare the two honestly.
You can switch between monthly and yearly at any time, and cancel from Settings ▸ Plan & Access without contacting us.

sections.title: Orders
sections.text:
Orders is the heart of NivaDesk: the list of every job you are working on. From here you create orders, find them quickly and open one to manage all of its details.
Opening an order shows a set of cards: Preview, Order Summary, Financial Info, Client Files and more. Each card covers one part of the job. You decide which cards you see and how they are arranged.
Select a card on the left to see exactly what it does and what you can change in it.

sections.title: Preview card
sections.text:
The Preview card is the visual header of the order. It shows the order image and your business logo, giving you and your client an instant sense of the job.
Tip: a good preview photo makes orders far easier to recognize at a glance in a busy list.

sections.title: Repair Intake & Item card
sections.text:
When a customer hands you their own item to repair, service or alter, this card is the record of what came in. It is deliberately not inventory: the item is stamped as customer-owned so nothing downstream can mistake it for your stock.
Tip: photograph the item at intake even when it looks fine. It is the cheapest possible protection against a disagreement about a scratch later.

sections.title: Customer Portal card
sections.text:
The question every repair shop answers all day is ‘is mine ready yet?’. This card is the answer: one link per order that the customer opens with no login, showing where their item is.
Internal notes, cost prices, supplier names, profit and team messages. These are not filtered out of the order on the way to the page — the page is built only from the parts you switch on, so nothing else can leak into it.
Tip: send the link when the item comes in, not when it is finished. Most of the calls you are trying to avoid happen in the middle.

sections.title: Production
sections.text:
The operations layer between Orders and Schedule. Orders says what a customer asked for; Schedule says when it must be ready; Production answers the question you actually ask each morning — where is every live job right now, and what has stopped.
Production status is deliberately separate from order, payment and delivery status. A job can be paid for, undelivered, and still sitting in Quality Check; keeping the three apart is what stops a workshop losing track of its own work.

Üretim Siparişler ile Takvim arasındaki operasyon katmanı. Üretim durumu; sipariş, ödeme ve teslimat durumundan bilinçli olarak ayrıdır. Bir iş ödenmiş, teslim edilmemiş ve hâlâ Kalite Kontrol'de olabilir; bu üçünü ayrı tutmak, atölyenin kendi işini gözden kaçırmasını önler.

sections.title: Etsy
sections.text:
Etsy is a connection of its own rather than a webhook recipe. You sign in to Etsy once, and your shop's orders arrive in NivaDesk with the buyer, the items and the personalisation notes already in place — so a made-to-order shop can work from its production board instead of living in the Etsy tab.
Nothing is imported behind your back. The first import is a preview you approve, and any order NivaDesk will not bring in tells you why in a sentence instead of disappearing quietly.
When the same buyer orders again, NivaDesk recognises them and files the new order under the customer you already have.
